results.mechanics_note: 45 questions / 60 minutes / scaled score of 70 to pass, per CPS HR's official exam FAQ. The real score is a proprietary scaled score (0-100), not literally percent-correct -- this uses raw percent-correct against the same 70 threshold as a practice approximation.

The real CA DMV Class C written knowledge test's format depends on the applicant's age -- confirmed against DMV's own 2006 Class C written-test evaluation report plus current (2026) corroborating sources: first-time applicants 18+ get 36 questions (30 correct/83.3% to pass), first-time applicants under 18 (provisional permit) get 46 questions (38 correct/82.6%). This entry is the 18+ format -- the default for anyone who didn't give an age at checkout or pick a category on the exam intro page (see CA_DRIVER_UNDER18_CONFIG + getExamConfig below). 30/36 = 83.33...%, using 83.3 (not 83) so a candidate scoring exactly the real pass line is graded as passing here too, same reasoning as the under-18 variant's 82.6. The real test is genuinely untimed (in-person at a DMV office/kiosk, confirmed against DMV's own testing-process page and that same evaluation report -- no time limit is mentioned anywhere). durationSec: 0 is this codebase's sentinel for "untimed" -- every consumer (findInProgressAttempt, handleExamAnswer, buildExamResult) treats a falsy duration_sec as "never expires" rather than computing against it.

Exact question count (50) is not spelled out in the manual text itself but matches the federally standardized 49 CFR 383.135(a) General Knowledge format and is corroborated by multiple third-party AZ CDL prep sources (epermittest.com, dmv-written-test.com); no official time limit found, 60 minutes is a generous stand-in per this project's convention.

CONFIRMED directly from dre.ca.gov and the official RE 425 Examination Description form: 200 questions, 4 hours, 75% to pass, single unified exam (no separate national/state portions), administered directly by the California DRE itself -- unlike most other states, no PSI/Pearson VUE vendor involved. CONFIRMED directly from the official Pearson VUE Texas Real Estate Candidate Handbook (#094400, Jan 2026) and companion State/National Content Outlines (#094401): 145 total items (85 National incl. pretest / 60 State incl. pretest), 240 minutes, $39 exam fee. Pass = 60/80 National (75%) AND 38/50 State (76%) -- two separate thresholds, not one blended score; this row uses the harder State threshold (76%) and the combined 145-question/240-minute format as the practice-exam shape, with 98 as an approximate combined-correct target. Notably harder than the salesperson exam (56/80 National, 28/50 State). Requires 900 hours qualifying+related education (incl. mandatory 6-hr Broker Responsibility course) and 4 years / 720 points of experience within a 60-month window -- confirmed directly from TREC's own page.

CONFIRMED directly from DBPR's official March 2024 Candidate Information Booklet PDF and DBPR's official broker-requirements page: 100 multiple-choice questions, 3.5-hour time limit (210 minutes), closed-book, administered by Pearson VUE for DBPR/FREC; 75/100 to pass (75%), materially harder than the salesperson exam's 70%. 12 content areas with exact official weightings (Real Estate Brokerage Business 43% down to Zoning/Environmental/Property Management at 1% each). Prerequisites confirmed: 24 months active licensure within the preceding 5 years, a 72-classroom-hour FREC-approved broker prelicensing course, and a 60-classroom-hour post-licensing course before the initial license expires.

NY DOS administers the broker exam directly (no third-party vendor) and reports results as pass/fail only -- no published item count or percentage score. The 150-minute (2.5-hour) time limit, $15 exam fee, $185 initial application fee, and 2-year experience (or 3-year general real estate experience) plus 152-hour education prerequisite ARE confirmed directly from dos.ny.gov. The commonly-cited 100-question/70%-passing figures used here for practice-exam mechanics are third-party study-convention estimates, not official DOS figures, and are flagged as such in ny_re_broker.json's handbookNote.

Pearson VUE administers PA's broker exam under contract with the PA Real Estate Commission (PSI stopped registering/administering PA candidates April 1, 2023, per the Commission's own pa.gov announcement -- Pearson VUE has been the vendor since). CONFIRMED directly from Pearson VUE's March 2026 PA Real Estate Commission Candidate Handbook (#093900): the broker exam is two separately-scheduled portions -- National (80 scored items, 150 min, 75% passing) and PA State-specific (40 scored items, 60 min, 75% passing) -- combining to 120 scored items and 210 minutes (3.5 hours) if both are taken; a candidate must pass EACH portion independently at 75% (60/80 national, 30/40 state). This bank went through TWO backfill rounds (378/100 = 3.78:1 final) -- round 2 (2026-09-02) independently live-verified every remaining REEB 16 and REEB 18 subsection word-for-word and confirmed a genuine, fully-exhausted content ceiling in Trust Accounts and Approved Forms; Drafting and Supervision Knowledge closed most of its gap but could not reach WB-11's contingency-clause text, which sits behind the Wisconsin REALTORS Association's members-only login wall with no public mirror. The 3.78:1 ratio (below this project's 4:1 new-track floor) is accepted as this track's practical ceiling, backed by concrete verified evidence rather than under-effort.

PSI Services LLC administers the SC Broker exam under contract with the SC Real Estate Commission (bulletin id 441, updated 8/27/2026): National portion 75 items (80 points), 120 minutes; State portion 50 items, 80 minutes; combined 125 items, 200-minute time limit. Passing requires 60 of 80 national points AND 36 of 50 state points independently (96/125 = 76.8% combined). The exam blends the same 75-item National portion template used across every PSI-administered state in this campaign with a 50-item South Carolina-specific portion (Commission and Licensing Requirements, Statutes Governing Licensees/Non-Licensees, Agency and Non-agency Relationships, Additional SC Statutes and Topics including a real attorney-only-closing rule under State v. Buyers Service Co., and Closing Details), grounded in S.C. Code Ann. Title 40 Chapter 57.

Pearson VUE administers the AL Broker exam under contract with the Alabama Real Estate Commission (AREC): National/General portion 80 items (2.5hr) + Alabama State portion 40 items (1hr) = 120 items, 3.5hr combined. Passing is a flat scaled score of 70 (0-100 scale), the same threshold for salespersons and brokers. Uses Pearson VUE's own separate 8-section/80-item national template (distinct from PSI's 11-section/75-item template used elsewhere in this campaign), shared with wi_re_broker's own national outline structure. Alabama State portion (40 items): Licensing Requirements 6, License Status 2, Broker/Company Licenses and Place of Business 6, Recovery Fund 1, Disciplinary Actions and Process 3, Estimated Closing Statement 2, Trust Funds 3, RECAD 5, Violations Which May Result in Disciplinary Actions 12 (largest). Grounded in Ala. Code Title 34, Chapter 27 and Alabama Administrative Code Chapter 790-X, primarily sourced via arec.alabama.gov after every other Alabama legal-research mirror (Justia, FindLaw, the state legislature site) was consistently blocked.

PSI-administered. 80 national (150min) + 40 KY state (90min) = 120 items/240min combined, 75% pass on each portion. PRIMARY-CONFIRMED via PSI's official Kentucky Candidate Information Bulletin. See scripts/tracks/ky_re_broker.json handbookNote for full sourcing.

Pearson VUE-administered. 80 national + 55 LA state = 135 items/240min combined, scaled score 75 to pass on each portion. PRIMARY-CONFIRMED via Pearson VUE's official Louisiana Candidate Handbook (#091900, July 2024). See scripts/tracks/la_re_broker.json handbookNote for full sourcing.

PSI-administered. National 75 items (80 points, some items worth 2 points) / 150 min + Oregon state 50 items / 90 min = 125 items / 240 min total, 75 percent required on EACH section separately -- confirmed via PSIs real candidate bulletin PDF (test-takers.psiexams.com/api/content/bulletin/3376). PSI-administered. 75 national (80 points, scenario items up to 2 pts) + 40 Iowa state (40 points) = 115 items, 180 minutes. Passing is a RAW POINTS threshold, not percent-correct: 60/80 national + 30/40 state, sections scored separately. pass_percent/min_correct here are practice approximations against raw item count (90/120=75%; 115*0.75=86), same convention as CA Notary/UT Broker/OR Broker. PSI-administered. 75 national (80 points) + 40 Mississippi state (40 points) = 115 items, 4 hours. Passing is LITERAL percent-correct, scored separately per section: >=75% national, >=80% state (higher state bar than most peer states) -- pass_percent/min_correct here use the lower national threshold as a practice approximation, since this site cannot represent two different per-section percentages on one blended item count. No Mississippi Recovery Fund exists (confirmed absent). Confirmed via MREC/PSI Candidate Information Bulletin (10/1/2023) and the July 2026 License Law revision. See scripts/tracks/ms_re_broker.json handbookNote for full sourcing.

Pearson VUE-administered UNIFIED exam (national+state content combined into one exam, unlike most other states split sections). 120 scored items (+10 unscored pretest), 4 hours (handbook only states a general 2-4hr range for all AR real estate exams; modeled at the top of that range). Passing score is a proprietary SCALED score of 70, not literal percent-correct. A failure requires retaking the entire exam, no partial retake. Confirmed via Pearson VUE Candidate Handbook #090400 (June 2026) and Content Outline #090402 (effective 12/1/2025). See scripts/tracks/ar_re_broker.json handbookNote for full sourcing.

Pearson VUE-administered. 80 national (identical bank/weights as UT/NV) + 40 Kansas state = 120 items, 4 hours. Kansas BRRETA flatly prohibits dual agency, defaulting to transaction-broker status absent a written agreement. Confirmed via Pearson VUE Candidate Handbook #091700 (April 2025). See scripts/tracks/ks_re_broker.json handbookNote for full sourcing.

Pearson VUE-administered. 80 national (identical bank/weights as UT/NV/KS) + 50 Idaho state = 130 items, 4 hours. Confirmed via Pearson VUE Candidate Handbook #091300. See scripts/tracks/id_re_broker.json handbookNote for full sourcing.

Pearson VUE-administered. 80 national (identical bank/weights as UT/NV/KS/ID) + 50 Nebraska state = 130 items, 4 hours. See scripts/tracks/ne_re_broker.json handbookNote for full sourcing.
